fidelity: F2a — Single-Diode I-V with Beta-Flux Photocurrent and Decay ODE
source: Olsen, L.C. et al. (1993) Nucl. Instrum. Methods Phys. Res. B 73, 139; Prelas, M. et al. (2014) Progress in Nuclear Energy 75, 117; Sun, W. et al. (2018) Appl. Energy 225, 390; Klein, C.A. (1968) J. Appl. Phys. 39, 2029 (pair-creation energy)

unit.name: Ni-63 betavoltaic cell with diamond p-n junction — physics-lumped single-diode model
unit.source: Olsen et al. (1993); Sychov et al. (2008) Appl. Radiat. Isot. 66; Prelas et al. (2014); Sun et al. (2018)

E_beta_MeV.note: Mean beta energy for Ni-63 (~17 keV; max 66.9 keV)

eta_capture.note: Geometric/self-absorption capture efficiency into the junction (~30%)

eta_collection.note: Charge-collection efficiency of generated EHPs (fraction reaching contacts)

W_factor.note: Klein factor: pair-creation energy E_pair ~= 2.8*E_gap + 0.5 eV (Klein 1968)

W_offset_eV.note: Klein offset (phonon loss term) in E_pair = W*E_gap + offset

I0_ref_A.note: Diode reverse saturation current at T_ref (wide-gap -> tiny I0); set so Voc ~1V at 300K

Eg_I0_eV.note: EFFECTIVE recombination activation energy in I0(T) law. NOT the full 5.5 eV diamond gap: using the full gap makes I0(T) vary 30+ orders of magnitude over 100 K and collapses Voc unphysically. ~1.5 eV gives a realistic, gentle Voc(T) slope across 200-500 K.

R_shunt_ohm.note: Shunt (parallel) resistance — high for good cells

FF_decay_rate.note: Radiation-damage degradation of collection efficiency (small for Ni-63)

C_thermal_J_K.note: Lumped thermal capacitance of the tiny cell
